source_record.bounded_interface_domain: A failure, maintained condition or recovery capability of the exact relevant asset supplies the named receiving technical/evidence premise. Arbitrary maintained office equipment is excluded. The named object, configuration, relevant time/population and actual receiving use are identified. Similar language, possible encoding, organizational co-use or an arbitrary tool does not establish a bridge. Unknown applicability remains unknown. A supported partial premise can be material while the whole receiving predicate remains unestablished.
source_record.domain_horizon_authority: The exact member object, configuration, observation interval, consequence and actual authority in each literal argument; no adoption or legal applicability inference.
source_record.evidence_ceiling: Sparse observations do not supply population failure estimates; maintenance does not establish arbitrary availability or safe recovery. Missing recovery does not erase a separately demonstrated reduction in exposed independent instances. Analytical native-role inference only; no empirical effect size, universal benefit, new historical descent or final scientific acceptance.
source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Maintenance labour and windows, downtime, spare stock, responders, configuration history, bad predictions, correlated failures, over-maintenance and single-expert dependency count. For a cheap noncritical item, run-to-failure with spares and tested replacement can be adequate.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: Generic co-use or arbitrary supporting tool rejected.
Whole receiving predicate failure does not erase a materially used partial input.
Every listed adverse control defeats the corresponding stronger whole-result inference.

positive_controls.argument: A consequence-based maintenance/recovery policy identifies observable failure and restoration requirements, plus the conditions a feasible verification method must test.
The actual failure and restoration dependencies identify interaction-level evidence needed beyond the maintained component's local pass.
The policy's actual degradation modes, downtime and recovery demands identify intended-use conditions that validation must examine.
Configuration and maintenance history can establish the actual state of the representative article and identify degradation or repair that changes qualification relevance.
Demonstrated restoration, identified spares and current maintenance evidence can support that bounded delivery criterion and expose an unresolved support burden.
A traceable maintenance/recovery policy and its evidence can support the specific applicable requirement where its means are accepted.
Failure history, policy assumptions, configuration and restoration evidence make the claim inspectable and reveal gaps such as single-expert dependence.
Versioned maintenance and incident records supply the identity and condition needed to locate affected claims, parts or service instances.
Consequence-based maintenance and tested restoration can address a named failure path or reveal that recovery itself introduces a hazardous transition.
Configuration-linked failure and restoration evidence supports a named reliability premise and retains degradation, common-cause and repair limitations as defeaters.
Diagnosis, replaced-component identity and restoration observations supply concrete anomaly provenance and a bounded basis for checking recurrence.
A tested recovery or replacement path, necessary resources and current configuration supply an actual readiness premise for the declared failure scenario.
Current degradation observations, maintenance actions and restoration evidence can maintain or defeat a bounded reliability premise over the relevant interval.
The policy's consequence model, actual restoration evidence and cost alternatives inform the real decision without manufacturing risk authority or acceptability.
